title: Find the Substring With Maximum Cost
summary: Given a string s, a distinct characters string chars, and an integer array vals, find the substring with the highest cost.
statement: Given a string s, a distinct characters string chars, and an integer array vals, find the substring with the highest cost. The cost of a substring is the sum of the values of its characters. The value of a character is its position in the alphabet if not in chars, or vals[i] if it is. The cost of an empty substring is 0.
constraints: A character's value is its one-based alphabet position unless chars assigns it the corresponding custom value.
A substring's cost is the sum of its character values; the empty substring costs zero.
Return the maximum cost among all substrings.
hints: Convert custom characters to a lookup table and use alphabet positions for the rest.
Track the best cost of a substring ending at the current character.
Either extend the previous substring or restart from the empty substring when the running cost would be negative.
This is Kadane's recurrence; the largest running value seen is the best substring cost.
editorial: This is Kadane's recurrence; the largest running value seen is the best substring cost.

tests.explanation: The best substring is aa with cost two.
Every non-empty substring is negative, so choose the empty substring for zero.
